subject: SCIENCE
title: Motion from a Reference Point
objective: Describe position and motion relative to a named reference point.
introduction: Is the ball moving? It was beside the cone, and now it is far away! How do we know something moved?

vocabulary.definition: An exact spot in space, marked with a dot.
The way something moves from one place to another.
A starting point used to tell where something is.

items.prompt: Which statement about motion is true?

options.text: Motion is change in position relative to a reference point over time.

items.explanation: To tell if something moves, compare it with a reference point, like a tree or a cone. Color cannot tell position, and you always need a reference point.

options.text: ball stays in a box all day

items.explanation: The ball changes its position compared with the cone, so it is moving. Staying in a box or changing color is not motion.

items.prompt: Which one is NOT needed to describe motion?
items.explanation: You need a reference point, like a tree or a cone, to describe motion. Without one, you cannot tell if something moved.

items.prompt: A ball changes from beside the cone to far from it. Relative to the cone, it
items.explanation: The ball's position changed compared with the cone, so it moved. Changing color or weight is not motion.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes position with a reference point?

options.text: book moves because it wants to

items.explanation: The book's position is compared with the box, so 'beside the box' uses a reference point. Feelings and wishes are not positions.
